findings.title: Deposit is within the amount cap
findings.detail: This amount check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. Annual rent GBP 15600; cap = 15600 / 52 * 5 (GBP 1500.00 rounded down to pennies); requested GBP 1500. Importance: 85/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Confirm that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The cap arithmetic holds up. Rent of GBP 1300 per month gives annual rent of GBP 15,600. Five weeks of that is GBP 1,500.00, and the stated deposit of GBP 1,500 equals the cap, so it does not exceed it. This is a correctly limited amount-cap pass. It says nothing about deposit protection or authenticity. The jurisdiction and tenancy type are unknown in the context, and the contract does not state the property is in England or that it is an ordinary private tenancy. Nothing in the contract defeats the calculation or the scope assumptions, so dismissal is not warranted. The rent (s5) and deposit (s6) appear to refer to the same tenancy, but the confirmation items on England, ordinary private tenancy and the same-tenancy scope remain unresolved. The conclusion therefore stays conditional on those facts. This is not a finding of breach. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants
